chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Talhah ibn Zayd who said:

I asked him about two men from the People of the Covenant or from the People of War, each of whom married a woman and gave her as dowry wine or pigs, and then they converted to Islam. He said: 'That marriage is valid and permissible; it does not become invalid because of the wine and the pigs.' And he said: 'When they convert, it becomes forbidden for them to give back to the women any of that which they gave them as their dowry.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْحَرْبِ: People of War (non-Muslims not under treaty)

ai.seo_question: Is the marriage of non-Muslims valid if their dowry consists of wine or pigs?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies that the validity of marriage (nikah) for People of the Book or War depends on the contract itself, not the purity of the dowry (mahr), meaning wine or pigs as mahr do not invalidate the union. Upon their conversion to Islam, the couple remains married, and the specific mahr given is not returned, illustrating the principle that conversion does not automatically dissolve prior valid marital bonds. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the essence of marriage is the agreement, while the mahr is a separate financial right that can be of any value.
